title: Faithful flatness in the middle of a composite of ring maps does not change tor amplitude over the base
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades the previous descent statement to an invariance: for ring maps R to A to B with A to B faithfully flat and a complex K of A-modules, the tor amplitude of K over R equals the tor amplitude of K tensor over A with B over R (statement lines 17261-17266). The proof is a 16-line computation (proof lines 17269-17284): it reduces the claim to the identity of cohomology modules H^i of K tensor over R with M, base changed along A to B, and on the other side H^i of the derived tensor product over R of K tensor over A with B with M, then proves that identity by representing K by a complex, choosing a free resolution of M and comparing two total complexes that differ only in the order of the tensor factors. The single point that a reader has to check is that the two total complexes appearing in the displayed equality are indeed equal, which uses only that B is an A-algebra and that tensor products commute with direct sums; faithful flatness is then applied exactly as in the preceding statement.
